newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air France at breakeven-paper interview.
newsitem.headline: Air France at breakeven-paper interview.

text.p: French state carrier Air France has an "excellent surprise" to announce in 1996/97 financial results on Thursday and is back to breakeven, deputy managing director Denis Olivennes told a French Sunday newspaper.
The airline, which is slated for privatisation, has not finished its modernisation programme but has got the economic fundamentals back into shape, he said in an interview.

"Air France is at breakeven," he said. "The 1996/97 accounts closed in April, which are to be published on Thursday, contain an excellent surprise," he was quoted as saying in France's Journal du Dimanche.
Previously, airline chairman Christian Blanc had said that he expected to narrow losses in the 1996/97 financial year to 200 million francs and return to profit in the following year.
Olivennes also said that the strikes and industrial turmoil of the past several weeks over wages, had cost the airline in the region of 200 million francs.
He said the airline had triumphed over the strikers, holding up concessions from two of three major trade unions as proof that the "extreme" element among protestors had lost out.
Cost cutting and improving commercial performance would continue, he said.
"Our goal is to be the best airline company in Europe within five years," Olivennes said.
